answer: Disjoint ingress neighborhood admission probes each agent’s two live entry points and hashes their /24 and AS-path neighborhoods against the active set. Overlapping entries are rejected unless they add a new disjoint network cell; a zephyr of benign churn gets only a short retry window. Timing jitter is checked against quartz clock skew to catch simulated routes. Each admitted identity thus needs separate AS egress and stable hosts, so mass registration pays rent, probe upkeep, and route-diversity costs. Shared hosting, however polished as marble, cannot supply the required separate cells.
